title: Resend Pricing 2026: Free Tier, Plans and Limits
summary: Resend pricing tiers—Free, Pro, Scale, Enterprise—set different monthly email allowances, daily caps, and per-thousand-email overage costs.
body_markdown:
## Resend limits that apply beyond monthly volume


Moving up isn't only about volume. A plan can stop you on a limit that never shows on the invoice. The limits are chiefly the daily sending cap, the domain count, the retention window and the API rate limit.


### Daily sending caps and rate limits


Count emails sent per day, not per month. A monthly allowance can look generous and still fail you if your traffic arrives in bursts.


A single product announcement or a batch of password resets after an outage can exhaust the day while the month is barely touched, because the free tier carries a daily cap on top of its monthly allowance.


For a production app, that means **the free tier is a testing tier** , whatever its monthly number suggests.


Separately, the API rate limit is a ceiling measured in requests per second. It shapes how you write your sender: a loop that fires one request per recipient will hit it long before a batch endpoint would.


Check whether your peak, not your average, fits under it, and queue sends rather than assuming a higher plan lifts it.


Activepieces can send your signup, billing and alert emails through Resend and watch for the bounces that come back, and it charges by the run: 1 credit per flow run, whether the flow has two steps or ten, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module.


A flow that sends, checks bounces and suppresses bad addresses costs the same as a bare send, so splitting the work into smaller, safer steps never raises the bill, and the free plan's 1,000 credits a month come with unlimited flows.


Every email the flow sends still counts against your Resend daily and monthly limits.


### Resend domain, seat and retention limits by plan


If you run one product, domains never matter. If you're an agency, or you separate staging, marketing and transactional sending onto their own domains to protect reputation, the domain count can choose your plan before volume does.


Domains are counted per plan, and the count steps up sharply between tiers.


When a customer says a receipt never arrived, a short retention window means you may have nothing to check. Retention decides how far back you can look at logs and message events.


Price it as a support cost. If you debug deliverability complaints after the fact, pay for the window that covers how long your customers take to complain.


### Resend dedicated IP and add-on pricing


A dedicated IP is sold as an add-on to the higher tier. It only pays off when your sending volume is steady enough to build the IP's reputation.


Last, read the attachment size limit. It caps what a single message can carry, so an app that emails invoices or exports should test its largest realistic file before choosing a plan, or link to the file instead.
